freshness.basis: Scheduled, not live. `tools/research/ingest_due.py` re-fetches this race's committed capture targets when the gap register's recheck date comes, at one request per second, honouring every robots policy. Nothing here is a timing feed and no figure here can be fresher than the last run that succeeded; the run history is published at data/ingestion.json.

attributed_sources.attribution: Weather derived from Open-Meteo, licensed CC BY 4.0.
Classification standings, stage winners derived from https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Tour_de_France, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_UCI_World_Tour, licensed CC-BY-SA-4.0.

withheld_verbatim_prose.reason: The organiser's roadbook sentences describing each course point are its own writing and its source is recorded all-rights-reserved, so they are not republished. Every figure they state — final-straight length, carriageway width, summit altitude, gradient — is parsed out and published as a number, and each point's position, category and kilometre are published in full. Facts about a public race are not the organiser's to withhold; its sentences are.

licence_policy.reason: Route GPX is retrievable but carries no redistribution licence, so only derived, simplified profile products are emitted; the source traces stay in the local vault.

simplification.note: Profiles are decimated for display and emitted columnar. emitted_points is always <= source_points; display resolution is never measurement precision. `decimals` is how many places each profile field is rounded to on the way out — a reader comparing these figures with a publisher's should know they are reading a rounded product, not the samples.

formulas.expression: summit = highest point of an ascending run, tolerating 40.0 m dips; foot = the start maximising H^2/(D*10)+(T-1000)/1000 among those with mean gradient >= 3.0%; kept if ascent >= 150.0 m and length > 500 m
formulas.description: Derived climb segmentation; never an official category.
formulas.limitations: Never an official category. The detector finds a minority of the climbs the organiser classifies and no setting in the swept 4x3 grid exceeds 61% recall, which makes the ceiling definitional rather than a tuning problem: a Cat 4 climb rising 90 m is below every threshold tested, and loosening far enough to catch it buys recall with false summits. A climb this project invented would be worse than one it missed. The foot is the harder half of the problem. A summit is a local maximum and is found; a foot is a judgement about where a climb stops being the road that leads to it, and this makes that judgement by maximising the published Fiets index over the starts that meet the minimum gradient. That is a defensible rule and not a measurement — a climb whose approach ramps gradually will have its foot placed later than a rider would place it, and the length and average gradient reported here are properties of the segment this rule chose, not of a segment the organiser named. Against the organiser own figures on the 19 stages carrying a classified list, the median disagreement is 0.45 km of length and 0.55 percentage points of gradient; those residuals are published per climb rather than averaged away.

formulas.expression: ascent over the stated climb length, from the elevation profile the product displays
formulas.description: Average gradient measured from the DEM, used to adjudicate between two published gradients for the same climb.
formulas.limitations: Reads the profile at the roadbook summit kilometre and one climb-length before it. Where the two publications also disagree about position, the sampled foot moves with the summit, so the measurement tests the stated gradient rather than the stated position.

formulas.expression: spread_m = max(elevation over DEMs) - min(elevation over DEMs)
formulas.description: Disagreement between independent DEMs at one route sample.
formulas.limitations: A spread requires at least two covering sources; a single-source sample has unknown spread, not zero. Resolutions differ (IGN 1-5 m, Copernicus ~90 m), so spread grows in steep terrain by construction and is not an error rate.

formulas.expression: elevation = RGE_ALTI(lon,lat) resampled every $2 m along the route
formulas.description: Elevation sampled from a national DEM along a 2D route line.
formulas.limitations: RGE ALTI covers France only; samples outside coverage are recorded UNAVAILABLE, never interpolated across the border.

formulas.expression: elevation = bilinear(Copernicus GLO-30 posts) at each route sample, thinned to one sample per DEM post
formulas.description: Copernicus DEM GLO-30 read from the published COG and sampled along the canonical route distance axis.
formulas.limitations: GLO-30 is a surface model: canopy, roofs and bridge decks are included, so a tree-lined road reads high. Heights are EGM2008 geoid, IGN RGE ALTI is NGF-IGN69 and a GPX trace states no datum; none is converted to another, so part of any spread is an unmeasured datum offset. A sample whose four surrounding posts are not all present is UNAVAILABLE rather than interpolated, and a tile that does not exist makes every sample inside it UNAVAILABLE.

formulas.expression: cumulative_s = Σ_stages (finish_time_s + penalty_s − bonus_s); rank by cumulative_s ascending; gap_s = cumulative_s − min(cumulative_s)
formulas.description: General classification from official per-stage results.
formulas.limitations: Requires a result row for every stage up to the reference stage. Does not model time cuts, jury time adjustments published only in communiqués, or team-time-trial time allowances beyond what the official per-stage result table already reflects.

formulas.description: Elevation change over a declared distance window.
formulas.limitations: A gradient is meaningless without the window it was measured over, and this one is a fixed distance window rather than a slope at a point. Short, steep pitches are flattened by it and a long shallow drag is not; two profiles with the same windowed gradient can ride very differently. The window is stored in the expression so a reader can see what was averaged, and no maximum gradient derived here is comparable to a publisher's figure measured over a different one.

formulas.expression: head of the official polyline remaining after trimming the official race distance backwards from the finish
formulas.description: Length of the neutralised/parade section preceding KM0.
formulas.limitations: Assumes the polyline ends exactly at the finish line and that the whole excess is neutralisation; a stage whose line is shorter than its official distance (repeated circuit laps) is excluded rather than fitted.

formulas.expression: window = [earliest published schedule, latest published schedule]
formulas.description: Official roadbook passage window; width is the uncertainty.
formulas.limitations: A property of the road, never a claim about any rider. The window is the interval between the organiser's own earliest and latest published schedules for that point; its width is the uncertainty, and it says when the race is expected to pass, not when anybody did. Nothing derived from it — weather, sun, wind — may be read as a condition any individual experienced.

formulas.description: Total ascent implied by the DEM profile, for comparison against the ascent the organiser publishes.
formulas.limitations: Diagnostic only, never published as a stage figure. Unthresholded summation inflates ascent wherever the profile rests on a single ~90 m DEM: stage 3 reads +39% with 539 of 981 samples on Copernicus alone. Thresholds of 1, 2, 5 and 10 m were tested; the 10 m floor needed to reconcile stage 3 takes stage 7 to -89%, so no threshold is right for both mountain and flat terrain.

formulas.expression: series and gender from uci_class; format from the published date range, or from the stage type for a championship event
formulas.description: Which published series a race belongs to and whether the product shows it.
formulas.limitations: Scope is a presentation decision, not a judgement about a race. An out-of-scope race keeps every byte of its evidence and is simply not published. Format comes from the calendar's dates rather than from a stage count, because a stage count this project has not collected would call a stage race a one-day race — a statement about the observatory dressed as a statement about the race.

formulas.expression: highest tier T such that every tier <= T is satisfied
formulas.description: Measured depth of holdings per registered race.
formulas.limitations: Counts rows held, which is not the same as rows that exist. A race at CALENDAR is one this project has not collected, not one that lacks entries or results. The tier is a statement about the observatory, never about the race. Claim and artifact counts come from a derived attribution that refuses to choose when an artifact serves more than one race, so evidence shared across races is counted for none of them.

formulas.description: How far two independently edited pages agree on who won each race.
formulas.limitations: Agreement is not proof: both pages can be edited from the same report, so this bounds transcription error rather than establishing the result. Names are compared without accents or case, so an orthographic difference is not counted as a disagreement.

formulas.expression: count(rank = 1) over held general classifications and held stage results
formulas.description: Victories per rider, team and nation across every race this project holds a result for.
formulas.limitations: Counts held races, never the season. A win in a race at CALENDAR depth is invisible here because nothing in this database records it, so races_seen is stored on every row and the two must be read together. Names are counted as published: two spellings of one squad stay two, because a rule that merged them would as readily merge two squads that differ.

formulas.description: Sun elevation and azimuth at a route point during its window.
formulas.limitations: Deterministic geometry for a point on the road during its passage window, not for a rider. It ignores terrain shading entirely: a sun elevation of 20 degrees says nothing about whether a valley road was actually in shadow, and in the Alps it frequently was. Computed at the window's midpoint, so a wide window makes the angle less representative in proportion to its width.

formulas.expression: hourly reanalysis at ST_StartPoint(published route), stage local day
formulas.description: Observed hourly weather at the point a stage started, for its whole local day.
formulas.limitations: A property of one point — where the stage began — and not of the route. A stage that climbs 2000 m ends its day in weather this row cannot describe, and a 200 km transfer across a range makes it describe the wrong side of that range for most of the stage. It is a model reanalysis, not a station reading: the grid cell it comes from sits some measured distance from the coordinate asked about, at a model elevation that may differ from the ground by hundreds of metres, and both are stored per row so the gap is visible rather than assumed away. Nothing here may be read as a condition any individual rider experienced.

formulas.description: Wind resolved onto route heading. A road property.
formulas.limitations: A road property resolved onto the route's heading, not a wind any rider felt. It comes from a model grid whose cell is on average 1 km from the road and up to 6.6 km away, at a model elevation that differs from the road by up to 224 m; it is a free-stream value with no account of shelter, trees, buildings or the peloton itself. Headwind and crosswind here describe an exposed road at a moment, and nothing more.

geometry.reason: The geometry layer states 185.5 km where the official stage distance is 154.6 km. The layer is carrying a superseded route, so its line is not used; the stage amendment is the fact here, not the distance. Third-party GPX length disagrees with the official stage distance by 31.009 km, so it is not this stage's route. Elevation profile, gradients, climb detection and distance-based waypoint positioning are all withheld for this stage.

The organiser shortened stage 21 to 89 km from 133 km on 25 July, after the Ministry of the Interior redeployed security forces to the wildfire response in the Gironde and elsewhere. The riders no longer race from Thoiry: the caravan parades and transfers, the teams are presented at Thoiry and travel to Paris by bus, and the race is started from the finish line on the Champs-Élysées at 17:50 for a scheduled finish at 19:45 local time (CEST), with the caravan leaving Thoiry at 13:20 and the teams presented there at 14:40. The 133 km route this project holds — its line, profile, 50 roadbook rows and every passage window, solar angle and weather sample derived from them — describes a course that will not be ridden, so it is retained as evidence of what was published and withheld from the product. A replacement itinerary has not been published in a form this project can capture. The official polyline measures 57.62 km against an official 89.0 km, i.e. shorter: the finishing circuit is drawn once rather than repeated per lap. Route offsets cannot be mapped to positions on this line, so it is not used as a distance axis. The line examined was published as 569 parts that cannot be ordered (parts meet at a junction where more than one continuation is possible); the single longest part was tested against the published anchors instead. Third-party GPX length disagrees with the official stage distance by 43.528 km, so it is not this stage's route. Elevation profile, gradients, climb detection and distance-based waypoint positioning are all withheld for this stage.

sources.name: Copernicus DEM GLO-30 (global 30 m elevation model)
sources.licence: Copernicus DEM licence (free use and redistribution, attribution required)
sources.note: Global 30 m elevation, read from the AWS Open Data mirror at copernicus-dem-30m.s3.amazonaws.com as Cloud-Optimised GeoTIFF, so only the tiles and blocks a route crosses are fetched. Anonymous HTTPS, no account, no key, no cost. The host serves no robots.txt (404), which RFC 9309 §2.3.1 reads as no policy published. Anything derived from it must carry the attribution: "© DLR e.V. 2010-2014 and © Airbus Defence and Space GmbH 2014-2018 provided under COPERNICUS by the European Union and ESA; all rights reserved." Held against the GPX-embedded elevation rather than replacing it: the disagreement between two independent series is the uncertainty this project publishes.

sources.name: Nominatim (OpenStreetMap search)
sources.note: Operated on donated infrastructure under the OSMF usage policy: at most one request per second, no bulk geocoding, and a user agent naming the application and a contact address. sources.note: Serves no robots.txt (400 on /robots.txt, an API-only host rejecting the path), which RFC 9309 reads as no policy. A demonstration server, so it is used sparingly and never in bulk. Its routes were refused on measurement and none is published.

sources.name: Overpass API (OpenStreetMap query service)
sources.note: Assessed and declined. A trial query returned usable road-surface tags, but robots.txt disallows /api/ for all agents, so the endpoint is not used. The data is ODbL and freely redistributable — the restriction is on this access method alone — and a bulk planet extract would be lawful. Mirror-hopping to another Overpass instance was considered and rejected as bad faith: the policy is the operator's, not the URL's.

sources.name: Overpass API mirror
sources.note: A community Overpass mirror that publishes no robots.txt, which RFC 9309 §2.3.1 makes permissive — unlike overpass-api.de, which disallows /api/ and is therefore not used. Queried once, tags only, to establish whether OpenStreetMap carries route relations for these races. It does not: of the relations whose names match, every one is a local cycle loop, a street called Vuelta, or a 1998 time trial. OSM maps permanent verifiable geography, and an annual race course is not that.

sources.name: Overpass API mirror
sources.note: A community Overpass mirror carrying the global OpenStreetMap extract. Serves no robots.txt (404), which RFC 9309 §2.3.1 reads as no policy published rather than as a prohibition. Used for MASTER_GOAL §7.F road surface, one query per stage against a route corridor, because it is the only reachable global mirror: overpass-api.de disallows /api/ in robots, overpass.kumi.systems stopped answering, overpass.monicz.dev returns 504, and overpass.osm.jp presents a certificate for another hostname. overpass.osm.ch answers quickly and must not be used — it is a Switzerland-only instance and returns HTTP 200 with zero results for a query about France, which would read as an absence of cobbles rather than an absence of coverage.

sources.name: swisstopo geocoding
sources.note: Swiss federal mapping. robots.txt disallows /dev, /checker and /mapproxy; the search endpoint is permitted. Used to resolve named Swiss course points during the §14 reconstruction attempt.

sources.name: Open-Meteo — historical and forecast weather
sources.note: Free API under CC-BY 4.0, which requires attribution wherever the data or a derivative of it is published. Terms fetched 2026-08-07 state a limit of 10,000 calls per day, 5,000 per hour and 600 per minute, and restrict the free tier to non-commercial use; this project is non-commercial. robots.txt is "Allow: /" for every agent. Redistributable with attribution, which is why the derived weather is published rather than withheld the way the all-rights-reserved route traces are.

sources.name: Climbfinder climb database
sources.note: robots.txt disallows only /dashboard/ for the general agent and publishes eight sitemaps. Its named blocks are AI-training and SEO crawlers — GPTBot, CCBot, OAI-SearchBot, SemrushBot and similar — none of which this project's user-agent matches, so the general group applies and the climb pages are reachable. Holds climb profiles rather than stage routes, so it addresses §5.3 corroboration and not the route gap itself; redistribution is not granted, so anything read here would be a derived product with the source named, as cyclingstage.com already is.

sources.name: Cycling Cols climb database
sources.note: robots.txt names ClaudeBot in its own group and disallows it, alongside GPTBot, CCBot, Bytespider, Google-Extended, Amazonbot, Applebot-Extended and meta-externalagent, and closes with a second catch-all group that disallows everything — contradicting the Allow it opens with. This project's crawler is not literally named there, but the operator has blocked every agentic client it could name and left the catch-all ambiguous, and an ambiguous permission is not a permission. Fetching under a user-agent the file does not name would be going around a stated restriction rather than reading one. Not fetched.

sources.name: komoot tours
sources.note: robots.txt carries 125 disallows for User-agent: * and none of them cover /tour/, /smarttour/ or /plan/ (measured 2026-08-08). Reachable. Same provenance question as Strava: a member's tour named for a race is not the organiser's course.

sources.name: La Flamme Rouge route database
sources.note: A public route database, checked under §12 step 4 for Tour de France Femmes 2026 geometry that steps 1 and 2 did not yield. It answers an interactive challenge rather than the page. Recorded as ACCESS_RESTRICTED and not worked around: defeating a challenge is outside what this project will do for a route file.

sources.name: Openrunner public routes
sources.note: robots.txt permits public route pages. Routes are member uploads and each is its uploader's copyright, so they are not used — the same ground on which Strava, Wikiloc and RideWithGPS were declined.

sources.name: Ride with GPS
sources.note: robots.txt disallows /*.gpx*, /*.tcx*, /*.kml, /*.csv, /routes/*/cue_sheet and /routes/*/elevation_profile for User-agent: * (measured 2026-08-08) — the export formats are the whole of what this tier would want. Not used.

sources.name: Strava routes and segments
sources.note: robots.txt permits /routes/, /segments/ and /activities/ for User-agent: * but disallows /api/ (measured 2026-08-08), so there is no unauthenticated programmatic path. Route provenance is the open question: a member-drawn route named for a race is not the organiser's course.

sources.name: VeloViewer
sources.note: robots.txt is served as 0 bytes (measured 2026-08-08), which under RFC 9309 states no restriction. Reachable. Its route data is largely Strava-derived, so the provenance question is inherited rather than independent.

sources.name: velowire race route articles
sources.note: robots.txt disallows only /admin. Publishes race routes as OpenStreetMap and Google Earth embeds; its 2026 Tour route article carries no .gpx, .kml or .kmz, so it offers no route file to take.

sources.name: Wikipedia — 2026 Tour de France
sources.note: Registered fallback for the classification tables that letour.fr serves only from robots-disallowed /ajax paths. Article path /wiki/ is permitted; /api/rest_v1/ is NOT, so the REST API is never used. Publishes top-10 only.

sources.name: Wayback Machine
sources.note: Publishes no robots.txt — /robots.txt returns 404, which RFC 9309 §2.3.1 makes permissive. Used only where a publisher's own address cannot answer: a lapsed domain, or a host this build's network cannot reach. What is read is the publisher's page; the archive is how it arrived, and the snapshot date rides with the claim.

sources.name: Lapsed domain — formerly Tour of Chongming Island
sources.note: Reachable and permissive — no robots.txt, which RFC 9309 §2.3.1 makes permissive — but not the publisher it is registered under. The deep path the infobox names returns 404 and the root now serves an unrelated betting site, so nothing here may be read as a statement by or about the race.
